name: Surge Module Manager
description:
Manage, categorize, refresh, and write Surge .sgmodule files in Module Manager. The Script-Hub tab uses the upstream Script-Hub beta conversion engine. It accepts remote URLs and local text, detects source formats, and offers previews and options for module name, filename, category, User-Agent, request headers, and advanced parameters. It supports imports into Quantumult X, Loon, Surge, Egern, Shadowrocket, and Scripting, plus one-tap writes for Surge modules. You can download remote resources referenced by [Script], RULE-SET, DOMAIN-SET, and #!include for offline use alongside the module. Scripts are saved to Surge/Script, and each script-path uses Script/<filename>. Rule sets and includes stay in the Surge root, and module files stay in their original locations. Every reference is checked against the actual filename. The remote URL basename serves only as the default filename. All writes stay within the authorized Surge directory and are verified by reading the file back. If a write fails, the original file is restored or the partial new resource is removed. For conversion links, resource localization uses the installed module as its first source to avoid mistaking the converter response for a Surge module. Scripting can import .sgmodule and .plugin files through its native import feature, using the existing proxy formats. Shadowrocket supports direct module imports. If a rule set cannot be opened directly, the result is copied.

The script opens with the Module Manager and Script-Hub tabs. There is no built-in online module catalog, third-party site list, automatic scanning, or third-party content distribution. When you request a conversion, the source content and parameters are sent to Script-Hub beta. Avoid entering sensitive credentials.

In Shortcuts, use Scripting's Run Script action to update modules. You can also use the system share sheet to send multiple Surge .sgmodule files to this script or a shortcut for batch import. Omit the parameter or pass all to update all remote modules, pass a category name to update that category, or pass JSON to select a category, directory, or module name. Batch resource localization writes files sequentially and skips toggling each module off and on, which avoids triggering Surge's protection against frequent reloads.

Advanced Surge controls are available under HTTP Remote Control. Use `/v1/policies/avoided` to temporarily avoid policies, `/v1/capture/filters` to filter captures, and the HTTP Capture controls to toggle capture or read saved sessions. The controls support X-Key and Bearer authentication and normalize the API address to `/v1`.

Select a valid bookmarked folder in Settings before running the script. If the bookmark loses access, the shortcut reports that the bookmarked path is unavailable.

localizedDescriptions.en:
Manage, categorize, refresh, and write Surge .sgmodule files in the Scripting tab. The Script-Hub tab uses the upstream Script-Hub beta conversion core, accepts remote URLs or local text, supports Quantumult X, Loon, Surge, Egern, Shadowrocket, and native Scripting module import, exposes advanced conversion parameters, and builds client import links. An optional setting synchronizes existing modules when saved, downloads remote [Script] script-path resources into iCloud Drive/Surge/Script, and rewrites each module script reference to Script/<basename>. RULE-SET, DOMAIN-SET, and #!include resources remain in the Surge root; module files are not moved. Every reference is verified against the actual local filename, and the remote URL basename is only the default name. All writes stay inside the authorized Surge directory and are read back after writing; failed writes restore the previous file or remove a partial new resource. Converter links use the installed module text first instead of treating a converter response as a Surge module, but this source fallback does not change the general naming rule. Turning the setting off and saving switches existing remote modules back to remote references while retaining downloaded files. Batch localization is serialized and does not force a disable/enable reload for every module. Native Scripting import accepts Surge .sgmodule and Loon .plugin files; Scripting is an import entry, not a separate proxy format. Shadowrocket modules can use the native import link, while rule-set results are copied when no direct import scheme is available.

The app has no bundled online market, third-party site list, automatic crawler, or redistributed third-party content. Conversion input and selected parameters are sent to Script-Hub beta only when the user performs a conversion action; do not enter sensitive credentials.

Shortcuts can run this script from Scripting to update all modules, a category, or selected names. Multiple local .sgmodule files can also be shared to this script or a Shortcut for batch import; each file is written and verified separately. Select the iCloud Drive Surge folder in Settings; the Module and Script subdirectories are created automatically when needed.
